result:
Renamed `totalAmount` → `grossAmount` across all seven files. Both modules pass:

- `mvn -o test` — BUILD SUCCESS, 1 test
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean; `vitest run` — 1 test passed

**Changes by layer:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `api/.../Order.java:15,27` | JPA entity field + `getTotalAmount()` → `getGrossAmount()` |
| `api/.../OrderDto.java:5,8` | Record component + the `of(Order)` accessor call |
| `api/.../order.graphqls:4` | Schema field on `type Order` |
| `web/src/generated/graphql-generated.ts:11` | Generated `Order` type |
| `web/src/lib/orders.ts:6,25` | `ORDERS_QUERY` selection set + `Order` interface |
| `web/src/components/OrderSummary.tsx:4,12` | Both read sites |
| `web/src/lib/orders.test.ts:9` | Doc comment only |

The DTO component name is what Spring GraphQL binds to the schema field, so `grossAmount` on both sides keeps the resolver wiring intact.

Two judgment calls worth your attention:

**I hand-edited the generated file.** `graphql-generated.ts` carries a "Do not edit — regenerated from order.graphqls on every build" header, but `web/package.json` has no `graphql-codegen` dependency and no codegen script (`build` is just `tsc --noEmit`), so nothing actually regenerates it. Leaving it stale would have left `Order.grossAmount` in the schema and `Order.totalAmount` in the checked-in types. If codegen lives in CI rather than the repo, re-run it and take its output over my edit.

**The database column name changes.** The entity relies on implicit naming, so the column goes from `total_amount` to `gross_amount`. There are no migrations or DDL files in the repo — nothing to update here — but against a real database this rename needs a migration, or an `@Column(name = "total_amount")` on the field to keep the old column. I didn't add either, since which one you want depends on deployment constraints I can't see.

Two test files carry comments saying they deliberately avoid naming the amount field so a correct rename won't break them; both held, which is why the passing runs above are meaningful rather than vacuous. I also ran `npm ci` in `web/` — dependencies weren't installed, so that was needed to verify at all.
